easy.def: To go in front to show the way.
examples: I lead the way to the door.
The guide led us through the cave.
A duck leads her ducklings.

more.def: To go first and show others where to go.
examples: The scout leader led the hikers up the trail.
A mother duck leads her ducklings across the road.
The guide led us through the old castle.

easy.def: To be in charge of a group.
examples: Who will lead the team?
She leads our club.
He led the class in song.

more.def: To be in charge of a group of people.
examples: Maya will lead the school band this year.
The queen led her people with kindness.
Who wants to lead the meeting?

easy.def: A soft, heavy, gray metal.
examples: Old pipes were made of lead.
Lead is very heavy.
Fishing weights are made of lead.

more.def: A soft, heavy, bluish-gray metal used to make weights and some batteries.
examples: Fishers use small weights made of lead.
Lead is very heavy for its size.
Long ago, many water pipes were made of lead.

easy.def: The person in front who shows the way.
examples: Today I am the line leader.
The leader of the band waved a stick.
Follow the leader!

more.def: A person who guides or is in charge of a group.
examples: A good leader listens to everyone on the team.
The team chose her as leader because she is fair.
The scout leader showed us how to build a fire.

easy.def: Being a leader.
examples: She showed leadership.
The team has good leadership.
Leadership is important.

more.def: The ability to lead a group of people.
examples: She showed leadership by helping the others.
The team has strong leadership.
Good leadership makes a team work well.

easy.def: A flat, green part of a plant.
examples: The leaf is green.
A leaf fell.
I found a big leaf.

more.def: One of the flat, usually green parts that grow from the stem of a plant.
examples: A red leaf drifted down from the maple tree.
Leaves make food for the plant from sunlight.
I pressed a leaf in a book.

easy.def: A small paper with facts or news.
examples: She handed me a leaflet.
The leaflet has pictures.
I read the leaflet.

more.def: A small printed paper, folded or flat, that gives information or advertises something and is handed out for free.
examples: Someone handed me a leaflet about the town fair at the park.
The leaflet explained how to recycle plastic bottles.
We picked up a leaflet at the museum entrance.

easy.def: A group of teams that play each other.
examples: I play in a soccer league.
The league has ten teams.
Our team is in a league.

more.def: A group of sports teams that play against each other.
examples: Our town has a youth soccer league.
The team won the league for three years.
Ten teams play in the baseball league.

easy.def: To let water or air out by accident.
examples: The pipe leaks.
The boat is leaking.
The roof leaked.

more.def: To let liquid or gas escape through a small hole.
examples: The pipe under the sink leaks.
The roof leaked during the storm.
Gas leaked from the old tank.

easy.def: A small hole that lets water or air out.
examples: There is a leak in the roof.
The leak is small.
The tire has a leak.

more.def: A small hole or crack through which liquid or gas escapes.
examples: A leak in the water pipe soaked the floor.
The plumber fixed the leak under the sink.
A leak in the tire let the air out.

easy.def: With a hole that lets water out.
examples: The boat is leaky.
A leaky pipe dripped.
My boot is leaky.

more.def: Having a hole or crack that lets liquid or air escape.
examples: The leaky bucket lost all its water.
A leaky pipe dripped under the sink.
Dad patched the leaky roof before the rain.

easy.def: To bend your body to one side.
examples: I lean on the wall.
The tower leans.
She leaned over to look.

more.def: To bend or slant toward one side, or to rest against something.
examples: I lean against the wall when I wait.
The tower leans a little to the side.
He leaned over to pick up the pencil.

easy.def: Not standing straight up.
examples: The leaning tower is in Italy.
A leaning tree is in the yard.
The fence is leaning.

more.def: Tilted to one side, not straight.
examples: The famous leaning tower in Italy is a big tourist attraction.
A leaning fence post needed to be fixed.
We passed a leaning old barn on the country road.

easy.def: To jump high or far.
examples: The frog leaps.
I leaped over the puddle.
The deer leapt the fence.

more.def: To jump a long way or high into the air.
examples: The frog leaped from rock to rock.
The deer leapt over the fence.
The cat leaped onto the shelf.

easy.def: To find out how to do something.
examples: I learn new words at school.
She learned to ride a bike.
We are learning to swim.

more.def: To get new knowledge or a new skill by studying, practicing or being taught.
examples: Children learn to read by sounding out letters and words.
He learned how to play the piano by practicing every day.
Scientists are always learning new things about space.

easy.def: A person who is learning.
examples: She is a quick learner.
The learner asked a question.
Every learner got a book.

more.def: A person who is learning something new.
examples: She is a quick learner who loves new skills.
Each learner in the class got a pencil.
The learners practiced their new words.

easy.def: A strap or chain that you hold to keep a dog close.
examples: I hold the dog's leash.
The leash is red.
The dog pulled on the leash.

more.def: A strap or chain attached to a dog's collar to keep it close.
examples: I held the leash tightly as the dog pulled ahead.
The sign says all dogs must be on a leash.
Our puppy chewed the end of its leash.

easy.def: To put a strap on a dog to keep it close.
examples: I leash the dog before the walk.
Please leash your dog.
We leashed the puppy.

more.def: To fasten a dog to a strap so it stays close to you.
examples: Please leash your dog before you enter the park.
She leashed her puppy and went out the door.
The owner leashed the dog at the busy corner.

easy.def: A strong material made from animal skin.
examples: My shoes are leather.
The belt is leather.
A leather bag.

more.def: A strong, flexible material made from the skin of animals, used for shoes and bags.
examples: My boots are made of leather.
The leather jacket kept him warm.
The baseball glove is made of soft leather.

easy.def: To go away from a place.
examples: We leave at noon.
She left the room.
The bus leaves soon.

more.def: To go away from a place or a person.
examples: The train leaves the station at nine o'clock.
Please leave the room quietly when the bell rings.
We left the beach before the tide came in.

easy.def: To let something stay where it is.
examples: Leave your shoes here.
I left my hat at home.
Do not leave the door open.

more.def: To let something stay in a place, or to forget to take it with you.
examples: Leave your boots by the door so you do not track in mud.
I left my lunch box on the school bus.
Please leave some cake for your brother.

easy.def: A long talk to teach people.
examples: The teacher gave a lecture.
The lecture was long.
We listened to a lecture.

more.def: A talk given to a group of people to teach them about a subject.
examples: The scientist gave a lecture about the stars.
The students took notes during the lecture.
The lecture was about whales.

easy.def: A person who gives a talk to teach a group.
examples: The lecturer spoke.
A lecturer came to our school.
The lecturer used slides.

more.def: A person who gives a talk to a group to teach them about a subject.
examples: The lecturer spoke about the stars.
A famous lecturer came to our school.
The lecturer used pictures to explain her ideas.

easy.def: A flat part that sticks out of a wall.
examples: The bird sat on the ledge.
The ledge is narrow.
I put my plant on the ledge.

more.def: A narrow shelf or flat part that sticks out from a wall, window or cliff.
examples: The bird sat on the window ledge.
A mountain goat stood on a narrow ledge.
I put my plant on the ledge in the sun.

easy.def: A soft, wormlike animal that lives in water and drinks blood.
examples: A leech lives in the pond.
The leech is slimy.
We saw a leech.

more.def: A soft, wormlike animal that lives in water and sticks to animals to drink their blood.
examples: A leech lives in the pond and clings to fish.
The leech has a soft, slimy body.
We found a leech on a rock in the stream.

easy.def: A long vegetable like a big green onion.
examples: The soup has a leek.
A leek is long.
Mom chopped a leek.

more.def: A long vegetable with a white bottom and green leaves, used in soups and stews.
examples: Mom chopped a leek for the soup.
The leek looks like a very large green onion.
The farmer pulled leeks out of the soil.

easy.def: On the side of the body opposite the right.
examples: Raise your left hand.
Turn left here.
My left shoe is wet.

more.def: On the side of your body that is opposite the right side.
examples: Most people hold a fork in their left hand.
The bakery is on the left side of the street.
She tied her left shoe, then her right one.

easy.def: Not used up.
examples: We ate leftover pizza.
The leftover soup is cold.
I found a leftover cookie.

more.def: Remaining after the rest has been used or eaten.
examples: We ate leftover pizza for lunch.
The leftover paint was stored in the garage.
She fed the leftover bread to the ducks.

easy.def: Food that was not eaten.
examples: We had leftovers for lunch.
The leftovers are in the fridge.
Mom heated the leftovers.

more.def: Food that remains after a meal and is saved to eat later.
examples: We had leftovers from last night's dinner.
The leftovers are in a box in the fridge.
Dad warmed up the leftovers for lunch.

easy.def: Food that is left after a meal.
examples: We ate leftovers for lunch.
The leftovers are in the fridge.
I like leftovers.

more.def: Food that is not eaten at a meal and is saved to eat later.
examples: We had leftovers from last night's dinner for lunch.
Mom put the leftovers in a container in the fridge.
Turkey sandwiches are a good way to use leftovers.

easy.def: A person who uses the left hand more than the right.
examples: I am a lefty.
The lefty threw the ball.
She is a lefty.

more.def: A person who uses the left hand more easily than the right.
examples: I am a lefty, so I write with my left hand.
The lefty pitcher threw a curve.
My sister is a lefty and uses special scissors.

easy.def: The part of your body you walk on.
examples: My leg hurts.
A dog has four legs.
She crossed her legs.

more.def: One of the long body parts that people and animals use to stand and walk.
examples: A spider has eight legs.
The horse stood on its strong legs.
She stretched her legs after the long drive.

easy.def: A part that holds something up.
examples: The table has four legs.
One chair leg is loose.
The leg of the bed is wobbly.

more.def: A long, thin part that holds up a piece of furniture.
examples: The table leg is wobbly.
The chair has four wooden legs.
The stool's third leg was shorter than the other two.

easy.def: Something left for those who come after.
examples: She left a legacy of kindness.
The legacy lives on.
The king's legacy.

more.def: Something that a person leaves behind, such as money, ideas or a good example.
examples: The author's legacy is her many stories.
The old teacher's legacy lives on in her students.
The park is a legacy from the first settlers.

easy.def: Allowed by the law.
examples: It is legal to drive at sixteen.
That is legal.
A legal sign.

more.def: Allowed by the law, or having to do with the law.
examples: It is legal to ride a bike on this road.
The park has legal parking spaces.
It is not legal to cross the street here.

easy.def: A very old story that people still tell.
examples: There is a legend about a dragon in this cave.
The legend is about a brave girl.
Grandpa told us a legend.

more.def: An old story passed down over many years that may or may not be true.
examples: According to legend, a giant made these hills.
The legend says a monster lives in the lake.
Many legends are told about the brave king.

easy.def: Famous, like a story from long ago.
examples: The legendary hero was brave.
The legendary tale is old.
She is a legendary singer.

more.def: Very famous, or told about in old stories.
examples: The legendary hero was brave and strong.
She is a legendary singer whose songs are known everywhere.
We heard the legendary story of a lost treasure.

easy.def: Tight, stretchy pants.
examples: I wore leggings.
Her leggings are blue.
Leggings are comfy.

more.def: Stretchy, close-fitting pants that cover the legs, worn for play or exercise or under a dress.
examples: She wore warm leggings under her skirt on the cold day.
My leggings are soft and comfortable for dance class.
He wore leggings under his shorts for the winter run.

easy.def: Laws made by a government.
examples: The legislation was passed.
They voted on legislation.
New legislation is coming.

more.def: A law or set of laws made by a group of lawmakers.
examples: The new legislation protects wild animals.
Lawmakers voted on the legislation.
Legislation about bike helmets was passed last year.

easy.def: A group of people who make the laws.
examples: The legislature met.
A state legislature.
The legislature made a law.

more.def: A group of people who are chosen to make the laws for a state or a country.
examples: The state legislature voted to build a new bridge.
Members of the legislature meet in the capital building.
The legislature passed a law about recycling.

easy.def: Free time to rest or play.
examples: I read in my leisure.
We swim at our leisure.
She enjoys her leisure.

more.def: Free time when you do not have to work or study, and can do what you enjoy.
examples: Reading is my favorite way to spend my leisure.
We walked through the museum at our leisure, looking at whatever we liked.
The new park gives families a place for leisure on weekends.

easy.def: A sour, yellow fruit.
examples: I squeezed a lemon.
The lemon is sour.
Lemons are yellow.

more.def: A yellow fruit with a sour taste that is used to flavor food and drinks.
examples: I squeezed a lemon to make lemonade.
The lemon tasted very sour.
She put a slice of lemon in her tea.

easy.def: A sweet drink made from lemons.
examples: I drink lemonade.
The lemonade is cold.
We sold lemonade.

more.def: A sweet, sour drink made from lemon juice, sugar and water.
examples: We sold lemonade at our stand.
The cold lemonade tasted sweet and tart.
She poured lemonade into tall glasses.

easy.def: To let someone use something for a while.
examples: I will lend you my pen.
She lent me a book.
Can you lend me a dollar?

more.def: To let someone use something for a short time and then give it back.
examples: I will lend you my pencil.
She lent me her bike for the day.
The library lends books for two weeks.

easy.def: How long something is.
examples: The length of the table is six feet.
Measure the length.
The length is five inches.

more.def: The distance from one end of something to the other.
examples: The length of the whale was nearly ninety feet.
We measured the length of the room.
The pool is fifty meters in length.

easy.def: A curved piece of glass that bends light.
examples: The lens is round.
I looked through the lens.
The camera has a lens.

more.def: A curved piece of glass or plastic that bends light, used in cameras and glasses.
examples: I looked at the ant through a lens.
The camera has a zoom lens.
His glasses have thick lenses.

easy.def: A big wild cat with spots.
examples: The leopard has spots.
A leopard climbed the tree.
The leopard hid.

more.def: A large wild cat with a yellow coat and dark spots that is a good climber.
examples: The leopard climbed the tree with its prey.
A leopard's spots help it hide in the grass.
The leopard crept silently through the bushes.

easy.def: A tiny man in Irish stories who guards a pot of gold.
examples: The leprechaun hid his gold.
A leprechaun wears green.
We read about a leprechaun.

more.def: A tiny man in old Irish stories who wears green and hides a pot of gold at the end of the rainbow.
examples: In the Irish tale, a leprechaun hid his pot of gold at the end of the rainbow.
The leprechaun wore a green coat and a tall hat.
On St. Patrick's Day, we cut out paper leprechauns and hung them on the wall.

easy.def: To make smaller.
examples: The rain will lessen.
Medicine will lessen the pain.
The noise lessened.

more.def: To make or become smaller or less.
examples: The rain began to lessen by noon.
Medicine can lessen the pain of a headache.
The noise lessened as the band walked away.

easy.def: Time when you learn something.
examples: We have a swimming lesson.
The lesson was fun.
The music lesson is at four.

more.def: A period of time when a teacher teaches something.
examples: I have a piano lesson on Tuesday.
The math lesson was about fractions.
She takes swimming lessons at the pool.

easy.def: Something you learn from an event.
examples: I learned a lesson.
The story has a lesson.
Never again, he learned his lesson.

more.def: Something that you learn from something that happened.
examples: He learned a lesson about being careful.
The lesson of the story is to share.
Missing the bus taught her a lesson.

easy.def: For fear that something might happen.
examples: Hold on lest you fall.
Be careful lest it break.
Hurry lest we be late.

more.def: So that something bad will not happen; for fear that.
examples: Hold the rail tightly lest you slip on the ice.
She whispered lest she wake the baby.
We hurried lest we miss the bus.

easy.def: To say yes to something.
examples: Mom let me stay up.
Please let me help.
Let the dog out.

more.def: To give someone permission, or to allow something to happen.
examples: My dad let me pick the movie on Friday night.
She opened the window to let fresh air into the room.
Do not let the cat get out of the house.

easy.def: Able to cause death.
examples: The poison is lethal.
A lethal snake.
The cold was lethal.

more.def: Able to kill, very dangerous.
examples: The snake's venom is lethal.
Some mushrooms are lethal.
The freezing cold was lethal for the plants.

easy.def: A note you write and mail to someone.
examples: I wrote a letter to Grandma.
The mail carrier brought a letter.
She mailed the letter.

more.def: A written message that is put in an envelope and sent to someone.
examples: She wrote a letter to her pen pal in Spain.
The mail carrier dropped a letter in our box.
He opened the letter and read it twice.

easy.def: A sign used in writing words.
examples: A is a letter.
Say the letter B.
Which letter comes next?

more.def: One of the symbols, such as A or B, that are used to write words.
examples: There are twenty-six letters in the alphabet.
Her name starts with the letter M.
He learned to write each letter.

easy.def: A leafy green plant that you eat in salads.
examples: I put lettuce on my sandwich.
The lettuce is crunchy.
We grew lettuce.

more.def: A leafy green vegetable with crisp leaves that is often used in salads and sandwiches.
examples: I put lettuce and tomato on my sandwich.
The lettuce in the garden grows fast.
Rabbits love to nibble on fresh lettuce.

easy.def: How high something is.
examples: The water level is high.
The river level rose.
Her reading level is high.

more.def: The height of something, or how much of something there is.
examples: The water level in the lake went down.
The noise level in the cafeteria is high.
Her reading level is very advanced.

easy.def: One part in a series of steps.
examples: I beat the third level of the game.
The parking lot has three levels.
She reached the next level.

more.def: One floor of a building or one stage in a game or a series.
examples: The parking garage has four levels.
I finally passed level five of the game.
Each level is harder than the last.

easy.def: Flat, with no bumps.
examples: The floor is level.
Put the board on a level surface.
A level field is good for soccer.

more.def: Flat and even, with no part higher than another.
examples: We set up the tent on level ground.
The shelf was not level, so the marbles rolled off.
The pool table must be level.

easy.def: A bar that helps you lift or move something.
examples: A lever helps lift a rock.
I pulled the lever.
The lever is long.

more.def: A bar that rests on a point and helps you lift or move something heavy.
examples: A long lever helped us lift the big rock.
I pulled the lever to start the machine.
A seesaw is a kind of lever.
